description: Wire routing into the end-to-end message pipeline (task P4.6, architecture.md Section 2.2): fill in the orchestrator-core/src/pipeline.rs placeholder to assemble message -> route -> provider -> tool loop -> persist. Build a RoutingRequest from conversation/persona/tags/override, resolve a RoutingDecision via the routing PolicyRegistry, resolve the provider adapter from the ProviderRegistry, stream the response, run the Phase 3 tool loop (attach MCP tools, handle tool calls with permission gating, feed results back, continue), emit MessageDelta/MessageComplete/MessageError CoreEvents, and persist the assistant message + RouteMetadata + TokenUsage on completion. Add an orchestrator-core integration test that runs a message end-to-end through routing to a MOCK provider and the fixture MCP server, asserting persisted route metadata + rationale and that the tool loop + permission gating work. Also add a `send_message(conversationId, content, overrideRoute?)` Tauri command (Section 8.1) that drives the pipeline and streams via Tauri events, plus a minimal typed frontend IPC wrapper - NO chat UI (Phase 5). Finally flip README Phase 4 status to DONE. Depends on FEAT-001 (routing API).
steps: Precondition: FEAT-001 is complete on the phase-4-routing-pipeline branch (routing engine API exists and routing is an excluded crate). Continue on the same branch.

orchestrator-core/Cargo.toml: it already path-deps routing/providers/mcp-client/domain/persistence. Confirm no new deps needed beyond what exists (serde/serde_json/uuid/chrono/thiserror/tokio; dev-deps async-trait/futures-util). If the pipeline needs futures-util in the NON-test build (to drive chat_stream's BoxStream via StreamExt::next), MOVE `futures-util = "0.3"` from [dev-dependencies] into [dependencies] (concrete literal, no workspace=true) and note it in the manifest comment. Keep the [[bin]] tool-loop-mock-server entry.

orchestrator-core/src/pipeline.rs (P4.6): implement the pipeline assembling architecture.md Section 2.2. Define a `Pipeline` (or `run_turn`) entry that takes: the SessionManager, a routing PolicyRegistry (or resolved active policy), a providers::ProviderRegistry, the set of connected mcp_client::McpServerHandle for the conversation, a PermissionGate/PermissionRegistry, the CoreEvent UnboundedSender, plus the conversation id and the new user message content and optional per-message ManualRoute override. Flow: (1) append the user Message via SessionManager; load the Conversation (privacy_tags, conversation_pref, persona_id) and its persona (via SessionManager.personas().get) if any. (2) Build providers::ChatMessage history from the conversation's messages (map domain Role/MessageContent::Text to providers ChatMessage; include the persona system_prompt as a leading System message when present). (3) Build a routing::RoutingRequest { messages, privacy_tags from the conversation, persona, manual_override (the arg), conversation_pref (from the conversation), available: from providers::list_available_models OR a supplied Vec<AvailableModel>, budget: None for now }. Resolve routing::RoutingDecision via the PolicyRegistry resolve(). On RoutingError, emit MessageError and persist an Error-status assistant message, then return. (4) Resolve the adapter: registry.get(&decision.provider_id) -> Arc<dyn ChatProvider>; if absent, emit MessageError + persist Error message + return. (5) Build providers::ChatRequest { model: decision.model, messages, temperature/max_tokens from persona ModelParameters, stream: true, extra: Null }. If a ToolBridge/servers are present AND the chosen model capabilities.tools, attach_tools(&mut request) (capability negotiation: omit tools when the model is tool-incapable, per Section 4.4). (6) Create a Pending/Streaming assistant Message id up front. Run the TOOL LOOP: call provider.chat_stream (fall back to chat + synthesize one delta if !capabilities.streaming), accumulate ChatDelta content emitting CoreEvent::MessageDelta per chunk, and assemble tool_calls from deltas. When the turn finishes with tool calls (finish_reason ToolCalls or accumulated tool_calls present), for each ToolCall run bridge.handle_tool_call (permission gating happens inside the gate), push the assistant tool-call message + resulting tool messages back onto request.messages, and CONTINUE the loop for another provider turn; cap iterations with a sane bound (e.g. 8) to avoid infinite loops (emit MessageError if exceeded). When the turn finishes without tool calls, it is the final assistant message. (7) On completion: build domain::RouteMetadata { provider_id, model, rationale, source } from the RoutingDecision, gather TokenUsage from the provider Usage if present, persist the final assistant Message (status Complete, route=Some, usage) via SessionManager.append_message, and emit CoreEvent::MessageComplete { status, route, usage }. Keep the module framework-agnostic (no Tauri). Add thorough //! docs (audit for doc_overindented_list_items). Derive Debug where tests need it; never Debug-format a trait object.

orchestrator-core/src/lib.rs: re-export the new pipeline public items (e.g. `pub use pipeline::{Pipeline, run_turn, PipelineError}` or whatever the implementation names them), keeping re-exports alphabetically ordered per convention.

orchestrator-core/tests/pipeline_e2e.rs (new integration test, P4.6 acceptance): build an in-memory SessionManager (Db::open_in_memory), create a conversation, and drive a message END TO END through routing to a MOCK provider and the bundled tool-loop-mock-server (spawn via env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_tool-loop-mock-server") exactly like tests/tool_loop.rs). Use a scripted mock ChatProvider registered on a ProviderRegistry (via insert_instance) whose id matches the RoutingDecision's provider_id, and a routing PolicyRegistry whose available models include that mock as a candidate (construct AvailableModel rows so autoDefault selects it, or use a per-message manual override to make the decision deterministic - prefer exercising BOTH: one test asserts automatic routing selects the mock and records source=Automatic + a non-empty rationale; another asserts a manual override records source=Manual). Script the provider: first turn returns a tool call for a namespaced fixture tool (server id + '__echo'), second turn returns final text. Assert: MessageDelta events were emitted, the tool loop invoked the fixture tool under PermissionMode::Allow (permission gating exercised), the final assistant Message was PERSISTED with status Complete, and its route metadata carries the expected provider/model + a non-empty rationale (and correct source). Add a variant asserting an Ask-mode permission blocks then unblocks via PermissionRegistry.resolve within the assembled pipeline. Do NOT use live network.

tauri-app/src/state.rs: extend AppState so the pipeline can be driven. Add the fields the send_message command needs that are not already present: a routing::PolicyRegistry (Arc-wrapped, active policy read from AppConfig.active_routing_policy at initialize, defaulting to autoDefault), and (reuse existing) session_manager, secret_store, core_events sender, permission_registry. If the provider registry / MCP server handles need to live on AppState for the pipeline, add them as Arc fields (build the provider registry from persisted ProviderConfig rows at initialize via providers::build_registry, mirroring list_available_models_inner; MCP server handles may be an empty/optional set for now since server-manager wiring is Phase 5 - document that the pipeline tolerates zero connected servers, in which case no tools are attached). Update AppState::initialize and AppState::new accordingly, keeping the existing constructor callers/tests compiling.

tauri-app/src/commands.rs: add a `send_message` #[tauri::command] with the Section 8.1 signature send_message(conversationId: String, content: String, overrideRoute: Option<ManualRoute>) -> Result<(), CommandError>. Validate conversationId (parse_uuid), content (non-empty, bounded by a new MAX_MESSAGE_LEN e.g. 131072), and overrideRoute (validate_manual_route when present). Factor the body into a `send_message_inner` (the established _inner testability pattern) that assembles the pipeline inputs from AppState (session_manager, routing PolicyRegistry, provider registry, permission_registry/gate, core_events sender, MCP handles) and drives the pipeline turn, streaming via the existing core_events channel (already bridged to Tauri events by events.rs / spawn_core_event_bridge). The command returns after kicking off/awaiting the turn as appropriate (streaming happens via events, per Section 2.2 'streaming delivered via events, not by holding a command open' - if the turn is awaited, ensure it does not block other conversations; a spawned task driving the pipeline is acceptable and matches Section 7.5 concurrency). Add unit tests via send_message_inner: rejects invalid conversationId/empty content/over-long content before touching the core (mirror set_provider_secret_inner tests); a happy-path test may be light given the offline constraint (heavier e2e coverage is the orchestrator-core integration test).

tauri-app/src/lib.rs: register `commands::send_message` in the tauri::generate_handler! invoke_handler list (this is what authorizes the command across IPC in Tauri v2). Keep the list ordering consistent.

frontend/src/ipc/commands.ts: add a typed `sendMessage(conversationId: string, content: string, overrideRoute?: ManualRoute | null): Promise<void>` wrapper over invoke("send_message", { conversationId, content, overrideRoute }), importing ManualRoute from ../types. Match the existing wrapper style/JSDoc. Do NOT add chat UI (Phase 5). Ensure the file passes prettier.

frontend/src/ipc/commands.test.ts: add a minimal vitest case for sendMessage mirroring the existing command tests (assert it calls invoke with the right command name + args shape). Keep consistent with the existing test structure.

frontend/src/types/index.ts: no new type is strictly required (ManualRoute already exists), but if send_message's overrideRoute or any new event field needs mirroring, add it keeping EXACT sync with the Rust serde shape (single-line unions if <=100 cols). Verify nothing drifted. (RouteMetadata/TokenUsage/MessageComplete already mirrored.)

acceptance_criteria: orchestrator-core/src/pipeline.rs is no longer a placeholder: it builds a RoutingRequest from conversation/persona/tags/override, resolves a RoutingDecision via the routing PolicyRegistry, resolves the adapter from the ProviderRegistry, streams the response emitting MessageDelta, runs the Phase 3 tool loop with permission gating (attach tools when the model supports them, handle tool calls, feed results back, continue), and persists the assistant message + RouteMetadata + TokenUsage while emitting MessageComplete (or MessageError on failure).

A minimal typed frontend sendMessage IPC wrapper exists. No chat UI is added.
